My family has farmed this land for generations. I never went to school but I know this soil — we sit on the North China Plain, and around here, everyone grows winter wheat then summer corn on the same fields. My husband goes to the city for work most of the year, so I manage our 8 mu myself, plus a small vegetable patch near the house.

I don't need to think too hard about what to plant. Wheat in autumn, corn after wheat harvest — that's what my neighbors do, that's what my mother did, that's what works here. Last year the wheat was decent, maybe 430 jin per mu after threshing. The corn was good too. I buy my seeds from the supply station in town — they push the Zhengdan 958 hybrid for corn, and for wheat I usually get whatever improved variety the station has, same as everyone else.

For fertilizer, I put down a base of compound fertilizer before planting and then top-dress urea when the wheat is jointing and when the corn is shooting. I don't measure carefully — I go by what I've always done and what the neighbor uncle suggests. Water is the worry. We pump from the deep well. I'll irrigate wheat maybe three or four times — before winter sets in, again at jointing, and at heading. Corn gets watered if it doesn't rain enough.

I'll keep 1.5 mu by the house for vegetables — garlic, cabbage, some tomatoes — mostly for eating and selling a little at the village market.
